The bug in the original code is that the keep_driving signal is set to the
complement of gas_tank_empty when arrived is false (0). This means that if the
gas tank is empty, the car keeps driving, even if the driver didn't arrive.

To fix this, we need to ensure that the keep_driving signal is set to 0 when
arrived is false (0), regardless of the value of gas_tank_empty.

Here is the corrected code:

```
module TopModule (
    input      cpu_overheated,
    output reg shut_off_computer,
    input      arrived,
    input      gas_tank_empty,
    output reg keep_driving
);

    always @(*) begin
        if (cpu_overheated)
           shut_off_computer = 1;
    end

    always @(*) begin
        if (~arrived)
           keep_driving = 0;
        else
           keep_driving = ~gas_tank_empty;
    end

endmodule

The bug in the original code is that the keep_driving signal is set to 0 when
the cpu_overheated signal is 1, regardless of the value of the arrived signal.
This means that the car will never start driving if the computer is overheated.

To fix the bug, we need to change the order of the two always blocks. We should
first check if the computer is overheated and set shut_off_computer accordingly,
and then check if the car has arrived and set keep_driving accordingly.

Here's the fixed code:

  module TopModule (
      input      cpu_overheated,
      output reg shut_off_computer,
      input      arrived,
      input      gas_tank_empty,
      output reg keep_driving
  );

      always @(*) begin
          if (cpu_overheated)
             shut_off_computer = 1;
          else
             shut_off_computer = 0;
      end

      always @(*) begin
          if (arrived)
             keep_driving = ~gas_tank_empty;
          else
             keep_driving = 0;
      end

  endmodule

The bug is due to the use of the negation operator in the sensitivity list of
the second always block. When the negation operator is used, the circuit
becomes combinational and all inputs are sampled simultaneously, which means
that the "arrived" signal can change between two combinational cycles, causing
the "keep_driving" signal to glitch.

The fix is to remove the negation operator. The "arrived" signal is sampled
every clock cycle, so the "keep_driving" signal will not glitch.

Here is the corrected module:

```
module TopModule (
    input      cpu_overheated,
    output reg shut_off_computer,
    input      arrived,
    input      gas_tank_empty,
    output reg keep_driving
);

    always @(*) begin
        if (cpu_overheated)
           shut_off_computer = 1;
    end

    always @(*) begin
        if (~arrived)
           keep_driving = ~gas_tank_empty;
        else
           keep_driving = 1'b0;
    end

endmodule

The bug in the original code is that the keep_driving signal is only set to ~gas_tank_empty when the car is not arrived. The signal should be set to ~gas_tank_empty regardless of whether the car is arrived or not. Here's the corrected module:

```
module TopModule (
    input      cpu_overheated,
    output reg shut_off_computer,
    input      arrived,
    input      gas_tank_empty,
    output reg keep_driving
);

    always @(*) begin
        if (cpu_overheated)
           shut_off_computer = 1;
    end

    always @(*) begin
        keep_driving = ~gas_tank_empty;
    end

endmodule
